events.title: Shakespeare's Othello premieres
events.description: William Shakespeare's tragedy Othello was performed for the first time at Whitehall Palace in London, before the court of King James I.
events.significance: One of Shakespeare's greatest tragedies, it still explores jealousy, race and betrayal on stages around the world.

events.title: The Great Lisbon Earthquake
events.description: A massive earthquake and the tsunami that followed devastated Lisbon, Portugal, on All Saints' Day and killed tens of thousands of people.
events.significance: The disaster shook European thought and religious faith. It also helped give rise to modern seismology and earthquake engineering.

events.title: Nicholas II becomes Tsar of Russia
events.description: Nicholas II took the Russian throne after the death of his father, Alexander III.
events.significance: He was the last Tsar of Russia. His reign ended with the 1917 revolutions and brought the Romanov dynasty to a close.

events.title: Assassination attempt on President Truman
events.description: Two Puerto Rican nationalists tried to shoot their way into Blair House in Washington, D.C., where President Harry S. Truman was staying. Truman was unharmed.
events.significance: The attack led to a major review of presidential security in the United States.

events.title: Maastricht Treaty takes effect
events.description: The Maastricht Treaty came into force and formally created the European Union. It also set the course for a common European currency.
events.significance: It reshaped European integration and paved the way for the euro.
